messages:
maria: FYI, Lyra (enterprise, VPC) just page'd us — sustained 5xx spike + latency from us-east dedicated pool. Customer reporting ~30% errors on inference calls. Starts ~1799199900 in their graphs. Paging now.
incident-bot: @channel INCIDENT CREATED: INC-1799200123 - Lyra tier: enterprise (VPC) | Impact: elevated 5xx & tail latency | Severity: P1 | Pager: kai_oncall | Runbook: /runbooks/tenant-failover.md :rotating_light:
kai_oncall: taking it. oncall etag: kai_oncall here, assigning roles: santhosh for runtime, evan for routing/dns, jen_sre for postmortem / comms. cs_amy you'll coordinate customer updates?
lyra_sre: Confirming — prod traffic from their EU and NA apps started erroring in us-east region. They see timeouts and 5xx from dedicated pool endpoints. No config changes from their side.
santhosh: grabbing pool metrics. quick check: `redwoodctl pool describe lyra-dedicated-us-east` -> look for queue depth / OOMs / kernel errors.
(santhosh posts): ```
$ redwoodctl pool describe lyra-dedicated-us-east
status: Degraded
available_instances: 0/4 (warm: 1)
queue_depth: 128
max_tokens_per_sec: 0
last_error: kv-cache OOM @ 2026-11-20T14:45:12Z
```
santhosh: looks like KV cache thrash + one node OOM, warm capacity is 1 which explains tail lat. I can spin warm instances in eu-west and start shifting traffic. Recommend warm->10, then canary shift 10%.
evan: DNS plan: Lyra uses per-tenant CNAME traffic routing with short TTL (60s). We can cutover by updating the CNAME to point to eu-west gateway behind a dedicated pool front. Steps: 1) ensure warm capacity in eu-west 2) update routing config (rollout: canary 10%, 50%, 100%) or 3) if TTL high, do edge-based proxy shift.
maria: their app caches DNS aggressively on some clients; ttl=60 but known mobile clients keep connections long. Can we do per-route canary via our routing layer instead of relying purely on TTL?
evan: yes. we have traffic-manager API to split percentages per-tenant. Example: ```
# set 10% -> eu-west
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/tenants/lyra/shifts \
  -d '{"policy":"weighted","variants":{"us-east":90,"eu-west":10}}'
```
cs_amy: I'll prepare initial customer status: "We are investigating elevated errors in us-east. We are warming failover capacity in eu-west and will execute a controlled traffic shift. Next update in 15 min." Sending now.
incident-bot: @kai_oncall 5min check-in reminder set.
kai_oncall: santhosh, runbook step 4 says scale warm to at least 3 before shifting. Can you confirm target counts and ETA?
santhosh: scaling now. ETA ~4m. Commands: `redwoodctl pool scale lyra-dedicated-eu-west --warm 3`
santhosh (2m later): warm instances active, health checks passing. CPU low, no OOM. Ready for canary.
evan: initiating weighted shift 10% -> eu-west. Running curl now.
neon-log: ```
POST /v1/routing/tenants/lyra/shifts 200 OK
{"us-east":90,"eu-west":10,"change_id":"chg-2337"}
```
kai_oncall: monitoring error rate. lyra_sre pls confirm if errors drop for the canary cohort.\lyra_sre: initial report: the 10% cohort is healthy, no 5xx. Error rate for remaining 90% still ~28%.\maria: good — proceed to 50%? let's hold 5 mins to ensure stability.
incident-bot: auto-update: metrics window 60s shows canary cohort lat p95 210ms, error 0.5%. Remaining cohort p95 1.8s, errors 27%.
jen_sre: taking notes for postmortem: probable root cause KV-cache OOM on us-east pool due to model change? we need to capture kernel logs and container OOM events. santhosh please save diagnostics: `redwoodctl pool collect-logs lyra-dedicated-us-east --since 30m` and upload to /incidents/1799200123/artifacts.
santhosh: logs collected and uploaded: /artifacts/1799200123/oom-trace.log. snippet: ```
[14:45:12Z] kernel: oom_reaper invoked for container 0x7f8b
[14:45:12Z] inference: kv-cache allocate failed: cannot reserve 1.2GB
```
cs_amy: Customer update: "We've shifted 10% of traffic to eu-west and are seeing healthy responses there. We're proceeding with controlled ramp. We'll update again in 10 minutes." Sending.
maria: moving to 50% now per plan. evan initiate 50/50.
evan: `chg-2338` -> 50% eu-west. response: 200.
incident-bot: metrics check: eu-west 50% cohort stable, overall error rate drops from 27% -> 12% in last 2 min.
lyra_sre: mobile clients still showing a handful of timeouts, but majority traffic healthy. No errors on eu-west.
kai_oncall: continue ramp to 100% if metrics keep improving for next 10m. Set rollback triggers: if error >5% sustained for 3 min, revert to previous ratio. jen_sre please capture RCAs requirements and action items.
jen_sre: noted. action items: 1) full memory profile of model (kv cache usage), 2) patch runtime to guard kv-cache OOM with eviction, 3) add per-tenant soft-limits, 4) expand warm capacity for Lyra's pool by default.
santhosh: after failover, I can repro locally with a sample workload to confirm OOM. will attach memory profiles.
(10m later) incident-bot: scheduled handoff at 1799200723: kai_oncall -> jen_sre.
kai_oncall: handing over to jen_sre for post-incident monitoring and PM follow-ups. All traffic is now on eu-west; us-east pool set to drain. Final actions from ops: scaled eu-west warm to 4, drained us-east, collected logs, customer notified.
jen_sre: taking over. drafting incident summary and timeline. cs_amy please send final update: "We have shifted Lyra traffic to eu-west and are seeing normalized error rates. We will continue monitoring and will follow up with a detailed postmortem and mitigations."
cs_amy: Sent update to Lyra's CSM and technical contact. customer ack: "Thanks, appreciate the quick mitigation. Please keep us posted on root cause and long-term fixes."
maria: closing notes: RCA likely runtime KV-cache OOM under specific model sequence patterns. mitigation: routing fallback + warm failover worked as expected. postmortem owners: jen_sre (lead), santhosh (runtime), evan (routing/dns).
jen_sre: next steps scheduled: runbook updates to include per-tenant warm thresholds, add automated canary for heavy models, and prevent single-pool OOM from impacting 100% traffic.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-1799200123 closed by jen_sre at 1799201923. Postmortem requested: /postmortems/INC-1799200123.md
jen_sre: thanks everyone. adding timeline to PM and scheduling follow-up with Lyra next week. :white_check_mark:
